name: Gorkha Bazaar (Town Center)
tagline: The walkable heart of Gorkha, shops, guesthouses, and daily life
description: The main bazaar strip is where most visitors base themselves: a cluster of guesthouses, general stores, tea shops, and bhojanalayas along a few sloped streets below the Durbar ridge. It's compact enough to walk end to end in 15 minutes and has the town's best (if still limited) wifi and mobile coverage.
vibe: Everyday small-town Nepali bazaar, unpolished and lived-in
bestFor: First-time visitors, short stays, easy access to buses and shops
pros: Most guesthouses and eateries within walking distance
Best wifi and mobile signal in town
Easy access to shops for supplies before trekking or onward travel
cons: Can be dusty and noisy near the main road
Limited late-evening options once shops close

name: Gorkha Durbar Ridge
tagline: The hilltop fortress-palace and temple complex above the bazaar
description: Perched several hundred stone steps above the town, Gorkha Durbar is the fortress-palace complex and birthplace of Prithvi Narayan Shah, unifier of modern Nepal, alongside the Kalika Temple and Gorakhnath Cave. The climb is steep but the reward on a clear day is a sweeping panorama toward Manaslu and Himalchuli.
vibe: Historic, quiet, physically demanding to reach
bestFor: History enthusiasts, photographers, clear-morning mountain views
pros: Genuinely significant historical and religious site
Best Himalayan viewpoint in the area
Uncrowded compared to Nepal's major heritage sites
cons: Steep climb of several hundred steps with no vehicle access
Views are frequently blocked by cloud, especially in monsoon

name: Bus Park / Lower Town
tagline: The transit hub below the bazaar, arrivals, departures, and shared jeeps
description: The bus park area sits at the lower edge of town along the road up from Abu Khaireni, handling buses and shared jeeps to Kathmandu, Pokhara, and surrounding villages. It's more functional than charming, with basic eateries and shops catering to travelers passing through rather than lingering.
vibe: Functional transit hub, busier and more transient
bestFor: Arriving or departing travelers, budget stays near transport
pros: Direct access to buses and jeeps without needing a taxi
Cheaper basic lodging aimed at transiting travelers
Easy to find quick, inexpensive meals
cons: Noisier and less scenic than the main bazaar or Durbar area
Further walk up to the Durbar and main shopping streets

name: Manakamana (nearby)
tagline: A hilltop temple town reachable by cable car, a common day trip from Gorkha
description: About an hour or two away by road and cable car, Manakamana is home to one of Nepal's most visited Hindu temples, dedicated to the wish-fulfilling goddess Bhagwati, reached by a scenic gondola over the Trishuli valley. It's a popular half-day or full-day excursion for travelers based in Gorkha.
vibe: Pilgrimage town, scenic cable car ride, day-trip energy
bestFor: Day trips, cultural and religious tourism, cable car views
pros: Spectacular cable car views over the Trishuli valley
Significant pilgrimage site with genuine local devotional activity
Easily combined with a Gorkha to Kathmandu or Pokhara transit day
cons: Can get crowded with pilgrims during festival periods
Limited overnight infrastructure if you want more than a day visit
